FIFA World Cup 26™ · Watch parties

Watch the World Cup on the big screen.

The final weekend of the tournament, live and outdoors under the Metrorail tracks. Two of the biggest matches of World Cup 26™ play on a giant Interstage LED wall — free, all ages, every flag welcome. Come in your kit, bring the crew, and make a day of it: food on site, a full bar, and a DJ keeping the energy up between the whistles.

Levitt BLOC Miami · Free Concert Series

Then the stage lights up.

When the final whistle blows, the music starts. The Underline's Urban Gym transforms into one of Miami's most exciting new music venues — a live headliner and a DJ crew each day, free and all ages, with food and drinks from local businesses plus pop-ups and activations all weekend. Same spot, same crowd, straight from the match into the party.

Sat Jul 18 · 7:00 PM · after the Bronze Medal Match

Palo!

Grammy-nominated Afro-Cuban funk · Miami
DJ set — Rum & Coke

PALO! is Miami's own Grammy-nominated Afro-Cuban funk band, built around the songwriting of keyboardist Steve Roitstein and the powerhouse voice of Leslie Cartaya. Their sound fuses Cuban rumba and son with funk, jazz, and soul into something entirely their own — bilingual, danceable, and unmistakably Miami. On stage they're a full live band with horns and percussion, the kind of set that turns a crowd into a dance floor. Expect originals, deep Afro-Cuban roots, and nonstop energy to cap off Saturday.

Sun Jul 19 · 5:00 PM · after the Final

Los Wizzards

Grammy-nominated Latin rock · Miami
DJ set — Walshy Fire, Neil Robertson + Supa Dups

Los Wizzards are a six-piece Miami ensemble that blends raw Latin rock energy with alternative textures — a sound that bridges cultures and generations. Grammy-nominated for Best Latin Rock or Alternative Album, they're fronted by vocalists Samy Hawk, Roy G. Robinson, and Teo Bok, backed by drummer Juseph Ballestero, bassist Rafael Querales, and cuatro player Wizzmer. Their live shows are pure party — big hooks, tight musicianship, and a groove that doesn't let up. They close the whole weekend on Sunday, straight after the Final.

On the decks

The DJ sets.

Between the bands and deep into the night — the selectors keeping both days moving.

Sat Jul 18 · after PALO!
Rum & Coke
Afro-Caribbean & Latin vinyl · Miami

A Miami collective — Jesus Rodriguez, Harold Fandino, and DJ Kumi — digging deep into Afro-Caribbean and Latin records of the '60s–'80s: cumbia, salsa, merengue, Afrobeat, soukous, and más. All-vinyl, all diaspora, straight from their Dante's HiFi residency.

Sun Jul 19 · closing set
Walshy Fire
Major Lazer · dancehall & global bass

Major Lazer's MC and a Miami-raised son of Jamaica, forged in the Black Chiney sound system. One of the best in the game at running a party — expect dancehall, reggae, and global-bass energy.

Sun Jul 19 · closing set
Neil Robertson
Selector · NYC / Miami

A selector splitting time between New York and Miami, with residencies at Dante's HiFi and SIP SIP. Deep industry roots and an easy hand across soul, funk, reggae, and global grooves.

Sun Jul 19 · closing set
Supa Dups
Grammy-winning producer · Black Chiney

Grammy-winning producer, Black Chiney founder, and hitmaker for Drake, Rihanna, and Bruno Mars. Behind the decks: reggae and dancehall roots with a pop producer's ear.
